title: Guide: parity circuits by CEGIS
description: The CEGIS loop with another specification: the parity (exclusive or) of m = 2 inputs. See the guide page "CEGIS: synthesis from counterexamples".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% A circuit of g two-input gates over the inputs 1 .. m. Nodes 1 .. m are the inputs, nodes
% m + 1 .. m + g the gates; the last gate is the output. A gate reads two earlier nodes.
inp(1..m).
gate(m+1..m+g).
node(1..m+g).
kind(and; or; nand).
outnode(m+g).
fragments.description: Part of the library example cegis-circuit.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% The synthesiser guesses a circuit: each gate's kind and its two inputs (A < B, both
% earlier). Every gate but the output feeds a later gate.
1 { op(G,O) : kind(O) } 1 :- gate(G).
1 { arg(G,A,B) : node(A), node(B), A < B, B < G } 1 :- gate(G).
used(A) :- arg(_,A,_).
used(B) :- arg(_,_,B).
:- gate(G), not outnode(G), not used(G).
#show op/2.
#show arg/3.

#program refine(k).
% The k-th counterexample input: cex(k,inval(I,V)) gives input I the value V, and
% goal(k,want(V)) the value the specification wants. Simulate the circuit on this input
% (w(k,N): node N is 1) and require the wanted output.
w(k,I) :- cex(k,inval(I,1)).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,and), w(k,A), w(k,B).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,or), w(k,A).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,or), w(k,B).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,nand), not w(k,A).
w(k,G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,nand), not w(k,B).
:- outnode(N), w(k,N), goal(k,want(0)).
:- outnode(N), not w(k,N), goal(k,want(1)).
fragments.description: Part of the library example cegis-circuit.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
glue(op(G,O)) :- gate(G), kind(O).
glue(arg(G,A,B)) :- gate(G), node(A), node(B), A < B, B < G.
fragments.description: Part of the library example cegis-circuit.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% The verifier: an input on which the circuit and the specification disagree.
{ x(I) } :- inp(I).
v(I) :- x(I).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,and), v(A), v(B).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,or), v(A).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,or), v(B).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,nand), not v(A).
v(G) :- arg(G,A,B), op(G,nand), not v(B).
out :- outnode(N), v(N).
% The specification (only the verifier knows it): the parity of the inputs.
ones(N) :- N = #count { I : x(I) }.
spec :- ones(N), N \ 2 == 1.
:- out, spec.
:- not out, not spec.
% The counterexample as data for the synthesiser: the input and the wanted output.
inval(I,1) :- x(I).
inval(I,0) :- inp(I), not x(I).
want(1) :- spec.
want(0) :- not spec.
#show inval/2.
#show want/1.
fragments.description: Part of the library example cegis-circuit.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# CEGIS (counterexample-guided inductive synthesis, Solar-Lezama et al.): the synthesiser
# proposes a circuit that is right on the inputs seen so far; the verifier looks for an
# input where it is wrong. Each such input is grounded in the synthesiser (Shape 3), which
# then has to simulate the circuit on it. The specification itself stays in the verifier.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.expand(refine, cex = X.atoms(inval/2), goal = X.atoms(want/1))
        count inputs
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))
